observations: No new photos were provided after the seller’s reply, so the visible condition/identity remains unchanged from the original 3 images.
The original photos still do not show a readable Toyota/OEM part number, engine code, or compatibility markings.

claims.claim: Engine oil pump balance shaft assembly for Toyota cars like Toyota Camry (2018–present) and Toyota RAV4
claims.evidence: No readable part number/engine-code compatibility markings are visible in the photos.
No invoice/shipping label or origin markings are visible in the photos.

claims.claim: Tested and working, no knock, low mileage, never opened
claims.evidence: Seller’s text asserts testing, but there is no test video/report or tamper evidence shown in the photos.

risks.risk: Wrong part / wrong engine variant (fitment depends on exact OEM part number and engine code).
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the stamped/engraved OEM part number on the casing (and/or Toyota number), plus the donor engine code/year.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially incompatible (worst case: buyer may not be able to fit it).

risks.risk: Not actually working or abnormal internal wear (external photos can’t confirm bearing condition or oil pressure/flow).
risks.proof: Short video of bench test or run test showing rotation and no abnormal noise; ideally oil pressure/flow reading.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not proven working (worst case: treat as needing inspection/possible replacement).

risks.risk: Leakage/seal failure (seals/gaskets may leak even if it “works”).
risks.proof: Photos of all gasket/seal faces and any weep marks, plus a wipe-clean test after a short run.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as may leak (worst case: assume seals may need replacement).

risks.risk: “Never opened” may be false (fasteners/seals could have been disturbed; not verifiable without tamper evidence).
risks.proof: Close-ups of bolt heads and gasket edges showing factory paint/torque marks or tamper evidence; any sealant lines.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as possibly opened/previously serviced (worst case: unknown internal wear).

proof_requests: Send 1–2 clear photos showing the exact stamped/engraved OEM part number on the assembly (and any Toyota markings).
Send the donor vehicle details: Camry/RAV4 year + engine code (photo of engine bay/engine cover where the code is visible).
Send a short video of the test (or a mechanic’s test note) showing it running/rotating with no abnormal noise.
Send close-ups of seal/gasket areas and any evidence of leaks (and ideally a wipe-clean after test).
response.reason: The seller’s reply is only a verbal assertion and does not replace the missing decisive evidence (readable OEM part number/engine-code match and proof of testing/condition). Without new photos or test proof, a reliable worst-case price can’t be set.
